lead.title: Victorian election 2026 live results: Ben Carroll projected to lose seat as Coalition wipes out Labor
lead.summary: Follow live updates and results tonight after ABC says Labor has no path to victory, with Jess Wilson to become state’s 51st premier Full report: Ben Carroll concedes Victorian election to Jess Wilson, ending 12 years of Labor government Victoria election live results: votes tracker, map and seat counts Victorian election 2026 guide: what you need to know Check the parties’ key promises and policies See all of our Victorian state election coverage Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast Federal politicians largely absent from state election Just following on from the last post, it is notable that the prime minister, Anthony Albanese , did not do a press conference with the state premier, Ben Carroll , during the campaign, and the federal Liberal leader, Angus Taylor , did just one press conference with his state counterpart, Jess Wilson , during the campaign. I give a shoutout to all those Labor party workers who are handing out how-to-votes, the candidates who are working their guts out, but they know that it’s going to be very, very tough. And we know that this election campaign has been dominated by really the sorts of issues that you get when a government’s been in for more than 10 years. Continue reading...

It is the key for my Tottenham. Maybe in the future with another coach this will change, but my Tottenham was born that day. That day it was tough to accept the defeat, tough to accept the behaviour after the defeat, but it was the crucial day and I have a great memory of the behaviour even though we lost the game, because I understood better what we needed at the time. Sports.title: South Africa have pushed the limits of rugby – time to show they still have the edge
Sports.summary: Rassie Erasmus has forged an iron bond in his squad but France could push them to breaking point at Twickenham At its best, Test rugby is a game played right out on the edge, where the players push the very limits of what anyone ought to be capable of. Out there the sport sells itself. In those moments it doesn’t matter if you know what a 50-22 is, or whether that was a hip-drop tackle or not, and no one needs a new Hemisphere Shield, or another message on the big screen telling everyone in the stadium to “Make Some Noise!” When it reaches that pitch of incomparable intensity, emotion and endeavour, Test rugby demands your attention whether you know it all or nothing at all. Stretches of this Nations Championship have been played out there, on the farthest reaches of the sport. Wales lived there for 80 minutes in their 35-28 win over the All Blacks a fortnight ago and were rewarded with one of the most famous results in their history. England came closer to it than they had been in a very long time during their own record 37-12 victory against New Zealand a week later. France got there when they were clinging on to their two-point win against South Africa in Paris, so did Ireland in the closing moments in Dublin days later, when they beat the Springboks by three and all the talk of a backlash be damned. Continue reading...

A former Athletic Bilbao captain coming up against an ex-Real Sociedad head coach needs no instruction on the importance of winning a derby, whether in the Basque country or on Merseyside. But this week, as the Liverpool head coach approaches his first experience of the latter, there has been no escape. “It has been very easy for me here,” says Iraola of his five months on Merseyside. “Family-wise we have settled in really well. Sports.title: Brit-splaining Botham and the impossible task of defining a sporting life without limits | Will Woodward
Sports.summary: Explaining the England all-rounder and now great-grandfather reveals a career that refuses to fit in a single box Across the Guardian sportsdesk this week it emerged that a young American colleague didn’t know who Ian Botham was. And why should she? She is young and American. And so the rest of us Brit-splained in five sentences, rehearsed here – and edited to make us sound better than we actually did. Botham is comfortably among the top five most famous living British sportspeople, certainly among those of a certain age. In 1981 he won (almost) single‑handed (arguably) the greatest Ashes series by bending it to his will. He was on the front pages as well as back in the 1980s, for soft drugs, suspensions and shagging. He is a member of the House of Lords. He is the most English of sports stars, Australians love him, and his grandson James plays rugby union for Wales, which is why we started talking about him. Culture.title: Sly, subversive and surprisingly modern: why Agatha Christie is still making a killing
Culture.summary: A century after her mysterious 11-day disappearance, the Queen of Crime is everywhere. With an exhibition at the British Library, a new Miss Marple novel and a hot young Poirot hitting the screen, how did the novelist become such big business? On the evening of 4 December 1926, Teresa Neele checked into the Swan Hydropathic hotel in Harrogate. A tall, attractive woman in her mid-30s with reddish hair and grey eyes, she had travelled from South Africa and carried just cash, a comb, a hot-water bottle and a photograph of a boy, the name Teddy written on the back. At dinner she told a guest that her daughter had died, and later danced the Charleston – “not very well”, according to those who were there. Neele spent the next 10 days shopping, going to the library, playing billiards and visiting the thermal baths. She placed an ad in the Times: “Friends and relatives of Teresa Neele, late of South Africa, please communicate. Write Box R 702.” And then, on 14 December, journalists and police poured into the hotel with news. She wasn’t Teresa Neele – she was Agatha Christie the crime writer, missing for 11 days from her Surrey home. Continue reading...
